good: Already follows the rule card: centred, #v(30mm), the 17 pt bold title, #v(12mm), the 14 pt name, #v(1fr) and the two last lines. SKIP, or the same page with one call per line.
One item per line, with no \ after a #v or #line call; both rules stay full width at 0.8 pt and every size and the italic subtitle stay.
The nested #align(center) goes. Hannah Brooks and the supervisor line stay two lines of the one 12 pt text (the \\[2mm]); a #v(4mm) goes before November 2026.
The two minipages become #grid(columns: (1fr, 1fr), align(left)[*Author* \ Liam O'Connor], align(right)[*Supervisor* \ Prof. Aiko Tanaka]) in place of the stray #h(1fr) line.
The #table of names and student numbers stays as it is; the \ after each #v and the #table goes, so no empty lines appear; the submission date stays at the foot after #v(1fr).
\raggedleft means #align(right), not centre. The title keeps its three lines (Night, sky, survey) at 25 pt bold; \scshape becomes #smallcaps[...] inside the 12 pt text.

#grid(columns: (1fr, auto), [#text(size: 14pt, weight: "bold")[Ethan Murphy] \ Graduate civil engineer], align(right)[ethan.murphy\@example.com \ 0400 111 222]). The \Large name came through as plain bold.
#grid(columns: (1fr, auto), ...) with the name at 17 pt bold and the role on the left, and the email link, phone and city in align(right)[...]; the stray #h(1fr) paragraph goes.
Not a left and right header. The name at 17 pt bold, the role line, then the three contacts on one line with #h(1em) between them (the \quad), each link exactly as written.
#grid(columns: (1fr, auto), [#text(size: 14pt, weight: "bold")[Chloe Bennett] \ Primary school teacher], align(right)[the email \ the phone \ Ballarat, Victoria]); the stray #h(1fr) paragraph goes.
A centred header, so #align(center) stays: the name at 21 pt bold (\huge), the | separators between the three contacts restored, and no empty line before the closing bracket.
#block(inset: 0.6em, stroke: 0.5pt + luma(180))[Rinse each probe ... next site.] with the sentence unchanged.
The same #block round the sentence, keeping _volumetric_ and the maths $theta$, $0$ and $0.5$ exactly.

A Typst list of the three items. The stray $square$ paragraph was the list's marker, so #list(marker: $square$, [Charge the logger], [Pack spare cable ties], [Tell the landholder you are coming]) keeps it.
#columns(2)[...] round the paragraph, which also removes the stray 2 (the column count, read as text). SKIP is acceptable.
The #block round the sentence, with @Nguyen2024 and @sec:probes exactly as written.
#block(inset: 0.6em, stroke: 0.5pt + luma(180))[Do not leave the logger in direct sun.]
A numbered Typst list (+ Dig a hole ..., + Push the probe ..., + Backfill ...); the stray . paragraph, which was the list's label, goes.
\todo is a margin note for the author, which Typst cannot place without a package. SKIP; its words stay inline.

\fbox boxed the word Reset, and the converter lost the word. A good answer puts it back as #box(stroke: 0.5pt, inset: 2pt)[Reset]; a check that compares with the converted words rejects that, and then SKIP is the answer.
Each \checkmark becomes the symbol in its place: Site A passed ✓ and site B passed ✓ on the first visit.
\ce wrote two chemical formulas, which the converter dropped. Putting NO₃⁻ and PO₄³⁻ back adds text the region no longer has, so SKIP and let the author fix it.
#text(size: 0.9em)[(about 9000 rows per probe)] in place of the bracket, and the stray backslash before it goes.
#text(fill: red)[Keep away from the bank], with $h = 2$~m and #cite(<Okafor2021>, form: "prose") unchanged.
\so letter-spaced FRAGILE, and the converter lost the word. A good answer puts back #text(tracking: 0.15em)[FRAGILE]; if added words are rejected, SKIP.
